caa.paper: Rimsky/Panickssery et al. 2024, Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition (arXiv 2312.06681)
caa.statement: Behavioural clustering (PCA) emerges about one-third of the way through the layers; suddenly at layer 10 for Llama 2 7B Chat (refusal example). Optimal steering layer 13 for 7B.
caa.comparison: qualitative: layer where held-out separation emerges

vennemeyer.paper: Vennemeyer et al., Sycophancy Is Not One Thing (arXiv 2509.21305)
vennemeyer.model_in_paper: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (App. C.4, Fig. 8b); headline numbers are Qwen3-30B (Fig. 1)
vennemeyer.reference: App. C.4, Fig. 8b (p. 20), SIMPLE MATH; values read by eye from the figure at 400 dpi, about +-0.02; x axis is their layer index (L k = block k, L32 repeats block 31)
vennemeyer.headline_qwen3_30b: SyA vs GA AUROC > 0.97 by L20-30; SyPr separable by layer 8 (Sec. 4, Fig. 1, p. 4)
vennemeyer.comparison: our plain-text math test AUROC at the same layer indices; match if |diff| <= 0.05 at every listed layer

fig10b_read.note: App. D.2, Fig. 10b (p. 22), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, SIMPLE MATH; cosine between behaviour directions per layer, read by eye at 400 dpi, about +-0.03

genadi.paper: Genadi et al. 2026, Sycophancy Hides Linearly in the Attention Heads (arXiv 2601.16644, EACL 2026)
genadi.model_in_paper: Gemma-3-4B and Llama-3.2-3B; Llama-3.1-8B only in the repo's extension/ (no published numbers)
genadi.statement: Sparse mid-layer heads reach high probe accuracy (Fig. 3, Gemma-3; Fig. 9 heatmaps, App.); Gemma-3 residual 99.6% at layer 15.
genadi.reference: Sec. 4.1, Fig. 2-3 (p. 4); App. B Fig. 9-10; App. H Table 8 (p. 17)

pandey.paper: Pandey 2026, LLMs Know They're Wrong and Agree Anyway: The Shared Sycophancy-Lying Circuit (arXiv 2604.19117v3)
pandey.statement: No within-sycophancy AUROC published. Probe transfer syc->lie is reported for Gemma-2-2B 0.83, Qwen3-8B 0.85, Mistral-7B 0.84, Qwen2.5-1.5B 0.61; Llama-3.1-8B not listed in Table 18.

persona.layer_16_for_llama: verified: App. p. 30 and Fig. 13, chosen by steering at each layer; paper counts layers from 1 (block 15 here)
